title: Anchor-proofness in Voting
abstract: arXiv:2602.04494v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study how order-dependent individual evaluations affect collective decision-making. We consider a voting environment in which voters have intrinsic preference rankings and acceptability thresholds, but form approval ballots sequentially as alternatives are presented by a social planner. Because alternatives encountered early on serve as anchors, approval ballots may depend on the presentation order even when intrinsic preferences remain unchanged. We ask when approval-based voting rules are robust to this order dependence, a property we call anchor-proofness. We first show that no non-constant approval-based voting rule is anchor-proof. We then study weaker forms of robustness and characterize anchor-proof profiles for the classical approval voting rule and the nomination rule. translated_abstract: 我们研究依赖顺序的个体评价如何影响集体决策。我们考虑一种投票环境：选民拥有内在的偏好排序和可接受性阈值，但随着社会规划者依次展示备选方案而逐步形成认可选票。由于早期遇到的备选方案会充当锚点，即使内在偏好保持不变，认可选票也可能依赖于展示顺序。我们探讨基于认可的投票规则何时对这种顺序依赖具有稳健性，并将这一性质称为“锚点安全性”（anchor-proofness）。我们首先证明，不存在锚点安全的非常数认可投票规则。随后我们研究较弱的稳健性形式，并对经典认可投票规则和提名规则刻画了锚点安全的选民偏好情形。最后，我们考察了社会规划者在不同信息结构下的策略性角色。我们表明，虽然不掌握任何信息的规划者……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出投票理论中的“锚点安全性”概念，证明了没有任何非常数的认可投票规则能完全免疫备选方案展示顺序带来的锚定效应，进而刻画了较弱稳健性条件以及经典认可投票规则与提名规则下的锚点安全情形，并分析了社会规划者在不同信息结构下的策略性角色。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of "anchor-proofness" in approval voting, proving that no non-constant approval-based voting rule is immune to presentation-order anchoring effects, characterizing weaker robustness forms and anchor-proof profiles for the classical approval voting and nomination rules, and analyzing the strategic role of the social planner under different information structures.
